Keeps coming back to Fedora because it often works best out of the box and has the newest software. Search results are not quite as good as for Ubuntu, but answers rarely fail to apply. Has run a home server on Fedora with in-place upgrades since about version 28 with no OS problems. Recently moved their daily driver from Windows; biggest complaint is Nvidia drivers.

Fedora became 'collateral damage' after the CentOS/RHEL drama; the user switched all personal systems to Debian. Says Fedora is excellent, but they don't have time to run different systems on personal machines and servers.
Running Fedora 39 on a new Framework AMD Ryzen laptop: relatively minimal hiccups getting it going, and it seems great now.
On low-end hardware, Fedora always freezes for minutes when RAM fills up; suspects ZRAM. Adding a swap file alongside ZRAM didn't help. Arch/EndeavourOS (zswap) runs much smoother for them.
Since fractional scaling got cut from GNOME, the user is holding off on Fedora Workstation 39 a bit longer.

Switched from Windows to Fedora Workstation on a laptop two years ago with no regrets, and also runs it on a home media server with Cockpit. Setup required a lot of searching and trial. Can't switch their desktop because of no Adobe support, missing 10-bit support, and CUDA; feels Linux isn't mature for professional audiovisual work.

Installing Fedora in VirtualBox glitched badly: every second letter was invisible and the desktop blinked as the mouse moved. Reddit said not to use Fedora with VBox (driver issue). Went back to Ubuntu/Xubuntu as more stable despite snaps.

Replaced Windows on a $480 Lenovo laptop with Fedora 39, and it became a full Python development workstation quickly. 'Everything just worked out of the box': Logi MX Master 3s configured and touchpad gestures working.
Has used Fedora as a daily driver since FC16. It was a bit shaky back then on a VAIO laptop, but they have stuck with it ever since.

Almost likes Fedora but specifically doesn't like the Workstation flavour. Built their own setup from Fedora Minimal by adding what they need, which was pretty usable. Would switch to Arch if Fedora favors Flatpaks over ordinary packages.

The Workstation roadmap's Flatpak focus turns this user away. Cites Flatpak papercuts: Adwaita-styled apps ignoring the distro theme, window resize controls not mapping, MPRIS not working, and config files in awkward locations.

Praises defaults like zram, fstrim, earlyoom/systemd-oomd, systemd-resolved, and btrfs with compression. Says the update GUI works reliably, even for release upgrades, making it worth recommending to friends and family. Debian's standard install feels behind by comparison.

Installing Discord or Spotify on Fedora took a page of commands and didn't run quite right. Some installed GUI apps didn't appear in the app menu and had to be added via the command line. Media thumbnails (ffmpegthumbnailer) were missing by default. Chose Pop!_OS instead.

Started using Fedora as a desktop right when it defaulted to Wayland and barely noticed the transition. The biggest issue years ago was screen sharing in Teams, which they can no longer remember being a problem; says the team has done well.
Likes that Fedora keeps pushing forward and switched to it for PipeWire for a while, but eventually went back to Linux Mint.
